axaHCkaUgd3KEy01DDeX.description:
When plants are destroyed quickly by natural disasters or deforestation, the remaining roots under the ground may come together to form eroots. By gathering themselves up in a giant, lumbering dirt clump, they remove themselves and roll around until they find a sufficient source of nutrients to feast. Often this results in eroots going to places of dense vegetation or farm fields then burrowing down into the ground to parasitize other plants. Unchecked, this chokes the life from other plants in the area and can cause a chain reaction of more eroots not unlike a zombie plague. Farmers are constantly vigilant for eroots infecting their soil, hiring adventurers if they have good suspicion that an eroot is in their fields.

Eroots do not use the dirt balls as just a mode of transport. By staying inside their spheres, the roots are not vulnerable to usual tactics of dealing with plants such as fire. New adventurers are often caught off guard by this, resulting in getting crushed by the eroots quick bowling strikes. It is suggested to instead break down the dirt by using ice and water then striking.

special.effect: When the eroot reaches **Crisis** for the first time after being hit by an **ice** attack, spell, or effect or any attack thereafter, it loses its dirt clump and reveals the spindly roots underneath. It loses its **Dirt Ball** attack as well as its Resistances to **Physical** and **Fire**. However, it also loses its Vulnerability to **Ice** and will Absorb **Earth**. If it regains health by means of Earth damage, it regains its lost attack, Resistances, and Vulnerabilities.
special.name: Erosion

bXXzYWVM6YGf1hkJ7uYO.description:
**Dancers** are peculiar creatures. Despite being one of the most humanoid forms of Nobody, they do not seem to be working toward any sort of intelligent goal. Instead, they use their cold, ethereal grace and humanoid familiarity to lull victims into a false sense of security so they can simply tear them to shreds.

**Dancers** generally appear in small packs, and the rare survivors of **Dancer** encounters have described their behavior as calculated deception. These **Dancer** packs will often appear a safe distance away from their targets and trail them for days, making no threatening moves. If these targets decide not to provoke them, they will approach frequently, as if harmlessly curious. Then, when it is clear they are not seen as a threat, the **Dancers** pounce. They seem to prefer ripping prey apart by trapping them in a *Captivating Waltz*.

Unlike Heartless, Nobodies have not been observed consuming hearts or otherwise benefitting from killing sentient creatures. This leaves only two possible explanations for the **Dancers'** cruel hunting patterns: some inexplicable compulsion, or a twisted sense of pleasure.


*Original art by Tetsuya Nomura.*

The **Dancer** twists and undulates with mesmerizing rhythm, gripping its target tightly and forcing them to join it in an eerie waltz. With each movement of the haunting routine, the **Dancer** slashes at its target with wicked claws.
On a successful Accuracy Check, the **Dancer** deals 【**HR + 10**】**physical** damage, and the target is unable to take Actions until the next round of combat.
